title: Sovereignty impact assessment and evidence patterns for cross-border model deployments
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Summary:
This page defines the 'Sovereignty Impact Assessment' (SIA) used to evaluate model-serving changes that may introduce new cross-border data flows, residency obligations, or different evidence requirements. It provides a reproducible assessment procedure, an evidence-pattern catalogue (what artifacts to collect), a retention/packaging schedule, and a decision matrix for risk acceptance and escalation. The guidance applies to hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to any model version, routing policy, or infra change that could alter the physical or logical location of inference inputs/outputs, logs, or derived artifacts.
- Includes model updates, new model variants (quantized or distilled), routing changes that move requests across regions, and export/replication workflows.
- Excludes purely local developer experiments that do not touch production capacity or customer data.

When to run an SIA (short checklist):
1) New model onboarding that includes non-U.S. training data or PII-labeled datasets.
2) Enabling a region (e.g., EU, APAC) for a model previously served only from US regions.
3) Changes to the audit/audit-log pipeline (new exporters, retention changes, redaction rules).
4) Introducing third-party plugins or connectors that persist inference outputs.
5) Any customer request for contractual residency guarantees or legal-hold support.

Responsibilities (owners):
- Requestor (Product/Platform owner): open an SIA request and provide deployment diagram, model artifact hash, and expected traffic profile.
- Security (policy and evidence lead): run the assessment, define the evidence bundle, and sign the acceptance.
- Infra/Networking: confirm network boundaries, egress points, and routing fallback behavior.
- Legal/Privacy: evaluate legal/regulatory acceptability and required contractual language.
- SRE/Oncall: validate runbook changes and rollback criteria for the deployment.

Procedure (step-by-step):
1) Intake & triage:
   - Create an SIA ticket in the compliance tracker with model_id, proposed regions, expected data class (PD0/PD1/PD2), and deployment timeline.
   - Attach high-level diagram (png/svg) showing ingress, serving tier, cache layers, and logging collectors.
2) Technical mapping:
   - Identify all persistent and ephemeral data objects for this deployment: inference inputs, outputs, KV cache, intermediate traces, aggregated metrics, and debug snapshots.
   - List their storage locations (region, bucket id, DB cluster id) and retention defaults.
3) Evidence pattern selection:
   - Use the catalogue below to select evidence artifacts required for regulatory proof and audits.
   - Mark any artifacts that need stronger protection (signed attestations, notarized manifests, HSM-backed keys).
4) Risk evaluation and decision matrix (see section below).
5) Packaging & automation:
   - Create an evidence bundle generation job (CI step) that produces the artifacts described and deposits them to the compliance evidence store.
   - If packaging is manual, schedule the packaging owner and runbook steps.
6) Approval & rollout:
   - Security and Legal approve the SIA; SRE runs a staged rollout with pre-defined monitoring thresholds.
7) Post-rollout verification:
   - Run evidence collection for the first 7 days and verify artifact completeness.

Evidence-pattern catalogue (artifact -> purpose -> minimum retention):
- Serving manifest (YAML): records model_id, model_hash (sha256), container image tag, commit id, compiled-kernel version. Purpose: provenance. Retain: 7 years.
- Deployment topology diagram (png/svg + MD5): shows region-to-region routes and egress points. Purpose: residency mapping. Retain: 3 years.
- Authorization logs (append-only audit stream): token_ids, policy decisions, subject attributes, resource. Purpose: proof-of-access decisions. Retain: 7 years (searchable index); raw stream retained 90 days.
- Network egress snapshots (netflow export): sample of flow logs for rollout window (first 72 hours). Purpose: demonstrate no unexpected cross-border egress. Retain: 1 year.
- Storage location attestations (signed): bucket/DB residency declaration including encryption-at-rest keys. Purpose: legal proof. Retain: 7 years.
- KMS usage ledger (HSM-backed): envelope key ids and key usage events for the model artifact. Purpose: key provenance. Retain: 10 years.
- Model artifact signing record (sigstore or internal equivalent): signature, signer identity, timestamp. Purpose: artifact integrity. Retain: 10 years.
- Redaction & de-identification checklist (md): shows fields removed/hashed before downstream storage. Purpose: PII control evidence. Retain: 3 years.
- Access-control snapshot (RBAC export): role bindings and attribute-based policies effective during deployment. Purpose: authorization evidence. Retain: 3 years.
- Sampling of inference payloads (sanitized): examples demonstrating classification/PII handling. Purpose: quality and privacy verification. Retain: 1 year (sanitized); raw never stored unless customer explicitly consents.
- Audit packaging manifest (JSON): list of all artifacts included in bundle with checksums and packaging timestamp. Purpose: reproducible audit. Retain: 7 years.

Decision matrix (high level):
- If any persistent artifact is stored in a region outside the contractually-required residency zone -> action: block rollout, require data relocation or encryption+key-escrow with customer control.
- If audit logs show non-trivial policy-deny events during staged rollout (>1% of requests with unexpected denies) -> action: immediate rollback and root cause triage.
- If network egress samples show unexplained cross-border flows -> action: quarantine, capture full pcaps for 24 hours, engage Legal.
- If model artifact provenance cannot be cryptographically proven -> action: rebuild pipeline with signed artifacts before deployment.

Retention and packaging schedule (textual table):
- Pre-rollout artifacts: serving manifest, topology diagram, RBAC export -> included in the initial evidence bundle and retained 7/3/3 years respectively.
- Rollout-window artifacts: netflow snapshots, authorization logs, KMS usage -> collected daily for 7 days, then aggregated indices retained 1 year / 7 years / 10 years as above.
- Post-rollout: audit packaging manifest and sanitized payload samples -> retain 7 years / 1 year.

Automation recipes (examples):
- CI job to generate a serving manifest:
  - Example (bash pseudo):
    echo '{"model_id":"${MODEL_ID}","sha256":"$(sha256sum model.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)","kernel":"${KERNEL_VERSION}" }' > serving-manifest.json
    sign-tool sign --input serving-manifest.json --key $CI_SIGNING_KEY --out serving-manifest.signed
- Residency assessment CLI (internal):
  - redwoodctl residency assess --model-id MODEL-123 --target-region eu-west-1 --output s ia-report.json
  - The command produces a recommended evidence pattern and a pre-filled packaging manifest.

Escalation and risk acceptance:
- Low risk (automated evidence available, all artifacts in-residency): Security approves; product may proceed.
- Medium risk (some artifacts require manual attestations or transient cross-border caching): Legal must sign a residual risk acceptance and SRE must add monitoring and an automatic rollback trigger.
- High risk (persistent storage outside allowed zones, inability to produce signed artifact provenance): Deployment is blocked until mitigations are in place; Executive Security must approve any exception.

Exception handling (ad-hoc evidence and timebox):
- Short-lived exceptions (<=72 hours): require an exception ticket with owner, compensating controls (encryption + key control), and an evidence sweep at exception close.
- Longer exceptions (>72 hours): require formal risk acceptance, documented residual risk, and scheduled audits every 30 days.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing RBAC export: mitigate by running automated RBAC snapshot and validating role-to-subject bindings before packaging.
- Unsigned model artifact: mitigate with immediate CI rebuild and automatic signing enforced by gating policy.
- Unexpected egress because of third-party telemetry: mitigate by blackholing telemetry endpoints in staging and ensuring telemetry uses regional collectors.

Checklist for evidence-ready deployment (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Serving manifest signed and checksummed.
- [ ] Topology diagram uploaded and MD5 recorded.
- [ ] RBAC export created and verified.
- [ ] KMS policy reviewed; key-escrow documented if required.
- [ ] Audit packaging job created and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Legal sign-off present for any cross-border storage.

Appendix A: example audit packaging manifest (JSON snippet described):
- The manifest must include: bundle_id, packaging_timestamp, artifacts: list of {name, path, checksum, signer}. Store manifest as text/json and preserve signed manifest in the evidence store.

Appendix B: retention FAQ:
Q: Can we reduce retention for low-risk models?
A: Any change to default retention must be approved by Security + Legal and recorded in the SIA ticket with business justification.

Appendix C: related artifacts and where to find them:
- Compliance evidence store: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/<project>/<bundle_id>/
- RBAC export service: https://internal-console/audit/rbac-export
- KMS usage ledger: query via KMS-ops team (ticket required)
